quantity.description: Change in own-team expected single-game scoring margin from adopting the strategy
quantity.support: unbounded real; positive favors own team

prior.consistency_check: Mode 0.6 lies inside [-0.2, 2.0]; skew-normal support is all real numbers, covering negative (backfire) effects. Quantile fit is approximate.

distribution_family.justification: The downside is bounded (worst case is roughly reverting to conventional decisions plus a few bad conversions), while the upside from consistently harvesting modeled EV is larger, so the interval is clearly asymmetric around the mode.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: Fit numerically: with alpha=2 the standardized SN mode is ~0.65 and central 95% quantiles are roughly (-0.55, 2.25); omega=0.8 gives interval width ~2.2 and xi=0.6-0.65*0.8=0.08~0.1, so mode ~0.6 and 95% mass ~[-0.34, 1.9], approximately matching my summaries.

strategies.rationale: Public WP/EPA models (nfl4th, Baldwin/Burke-style analyses) consistently show teams punt and kick far too often; capturing even most of the modeled surplus adds meaningful expected points and win probability over a season, and the edge is largest in close games where marginal points matter most.
strategies.recommendation: Go for it on fourth down whenever win-probability models show going for it is at least break-even, especially 4th-and-short between the opponent 45 and their 35 and near the goal line, instead of punting or kicking short field goals.
strategies.title: Model-Driven Fourth-Down Aggression

prior.consistency_check: Mode 0.4 lies inside [-0.4, 1.2]; normal support is all real numbers, covering signed effects.

distribution_family.justification: Uncertainty is roughly symmetric — defenses may partially adapt (downside) or the per-play EPA gap may transfer nearly intact (upside) — with no strong reason to expect extreme surprises.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: mu = most_plausible = 0.4; sigma = (1.2 - (-0.4)) / 3.92 = 1.6 / 3.92 = 0.408, using the 1.96 normal critical value.

strategies.rationale: Published EPA research repeatedly shows early-down passes and play-action dropbacks outperform standard runs by a wide per-play margin, and that play-action efficiency does not require an established run game; shifting the play mix converts more drives into scores.
strategies.recommendation: Raise pass rate on first and second down in neutral game states (roughly to a 60-65% early-down pass rate) and increase play-action usage toward 30%+ of dropbacks, cutting low-value first-down runs into stacked boxes.
strategies.title: Early-Down Pass and Play-Action Rate Increase

prior.consistency_check: Mode 0.3 lies inside [-0.6, 1.2]; normal support is all real numbers, covering signed effects.

distribution_family.justification: The effect depends symmetrically on personnel fit — a weak four-man rush could make passivity costly, while good coverage talent could amplify the gain — with no strong asymmetry or fat-tail mechanism.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: mu = most_plausible = 0.3; sigma = (1.2 - (-0.6)) / 3.92 = 1.8 / 3.92 = 0.459, using the 1.96 normal critical value.

strategies.rationale: Analytics on defensive EPA shows explosive pass plays drive scoring far more than incremental rushing yards, and blitzes on average concede more EPA than four-man rushes with coverage help; trading small run losses for fewer explosives lowers opponent expected points.
strategies.recommendation: Cut blitz rate to the league's low end and default to two-high, light-box structures in neutral and passing situations, rushing four and prioritizing prevention of explosive passes even at the cost of extra short runs.
strategies.title: Blitz Less, Play More Two-High Coverage

prior.consistency_check: Mode 0.05 lies inside [-0.25, 0.35]; normal support is all real numbers, covering the honest possibility this backfires. This is admittedly the weakest cell and the prior reflects that.

distribution_family.justification: This is a low-frequency, small-stakes decision; the plausible effect is near zero in either direction with no mechanism for a large surprise, so a light-tailed symmetric family fits.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: mu = most_plausible = 0.05; sigma = (0.35 - (-0.25)) / 3.92 = 0.6 / 3.92 = 0.153, using the 1.96 normal critical value.

strategies.rationale: My judgment is that 5 yards of punter workspace is worth more than 5 yards of field position in this specific zone because touchbacks destroy pin value; public analytics is essentially silent or anecdotal on this micro-decision, so this rests on coaching feel about punter behavior, which is why it is intuition rather than analytics.
strategies.recommendation: When punting from between midfield and the opponent 40, deliberately take a 5-yard delay-of-game penalty to give the punter more operating room and reduce touchback risk, aiming to pin inside the 10 rather than the 20.
strategies.title: Intentional Delay-of-Game Before Plus-Territory Punts

prior.consistency_check: Mode 0.3 lies inside [-1.1, 1.7]; Student-t support is all real numbers, covering signed effects.

distribution_family.justification: Tempo effects could plausibly be much larger than expected in either direction — trapping defenses in bad personnel, or shortening drives and exhausting my own defense — so I want heavy tails around a roughly symmetric center.
distribution_family.name: student_t

parameters.conversion_note: nu = 5 chosen for clearly heavy tails; t_{0.975,5} = 2.571; mu = most_plausible = 0.3; sigma = (1.7 - (-1.1)) / (2 * 2.571) = 2.8 / 5.142 = 0.545 (scale parameter, not SD).

strategies.rationale: My coaching read is that defenses are most vulnerable in the 40 seconds after an explosive play (fatigue, personnel mismatch, disguise breakdown); public analytics on tempo is genuinely mixed — it confounds team quality and game state and has no clean causal estimate of conditional tempo — so this is judgment, not established analytics.
strategies.recommendation: Pre-script 3-play no-huddle bursts triggered immediately after any gain of 15+ yards, attacking before the defense can substitute, align, or communicate, then reverting to normal tempo.
strategies.title: Scripted Tempo Bursts After Explosive Plays

prior.consistency_check: Mode 0.15 lies inside [-0.7, 1.0]; normal support is all real numbers, covering the possibility the vacated coverage costs more than the spy saves.

distribution_family.justification: Removing a coverage defender could hurt roughly as easily as removing scramble yardage helps, and the situational frequency caps the magnitude, so a symmetric moderate-tailed family matches my belief.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: mu = most_plausible = 0.15; sigma = (1.0 - (-0.7)) / 3.92 = 1.7 / 3.92 = 0.434, using the 1.96 normal critical value.

strategies.rationale: Scramble conversions on late downs are drive-extending, momentum-swinging plays that I believe standard coverage systematically underweights; public analytics has no reliable causal estimate of spy usage (usage data is sparse and scheme-confounded), so this sits on film-based judgment rather than an analytics consensus.
strategies.recommendation: Against top scrambling quarterbacks, assign the defense's fastest off-ball player as a dedicated spy on 3rd/4th-and-medium-plus, rushing four with the spy mirroring the QB rather than dropping into a standard zone.
strategies.title: Dedicated Elite-Athlete QB Spy on Late Downs vs Mobile QBs
